page: Amazon Web Services r8i.large is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. The processor runs at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes a massive 480 MB L3 cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8i.large exhibits strong single-core capabilities. It achieves high marks in single-threaded tasks, including Geekbench single-core tests, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression. However, because the instance is limited to a single physical core (2 vCPUs), its multi-core performance is constrained, as evidenced by lower scores in multi-threaded stress-ng tests, software compilation, and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth for large, uncached blocks also shows weaker throughput, though the DDR5 memory maintains a stable average PassMark memory score.

This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8i.large serves as a low-overhead entry point into the memory-optimized Gen8 family. It allows workloads requiring high memory capacity per core to run without the expense of provisioning larger multi-core instances.

The r8i.large is best suited for memory-sensitive workloads with low parallel processing demands. Appropriate use cases include small-scale database operations, single-threaded text and data processing, caching layers, and lightweight language model text generation using small models.

Powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, this x86_64 instance provides a dedicated CPU allocation with 1 physical core and 2 threads. While it lacks local storage and GPUs, it features a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks show strong single-core performance in text processing and compression, though multi-core scaling and uncached memory bandwidth are limited. With a baseline network speed of 1 Gbps, the r8i.large is a cost-effective option for memory-intensive, single-threaded applications, small databases, and lightweight caching layers.
